- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or mixed, model often underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 5–10 days if price is trending up.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–3 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% above recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model lags in capturing the reversal; adjust forecast to rise 1–3% per day for next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 10–30 day horizons; if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5) and price is volatile, model tends to over-smooth; add 1–2% volatility buffer to forecast for next 7–14 days.
